_comment: W09-VFX (CL-A2, funded by the owner 2026-09-04). Combat and reward VFX: the hit spark and body flash on every landed blow, the KO puff, the catch-success burst and the level-up flourish. ALL of this is tunable presentation; nothing here touches damage, reach, timing or progression. `enabled` false is the whole revert -- the existing impact_flash.gd ring in combat.json `impact` is independent and keeps playing either way. Sizes are in metres BEFORE the struck body's own radius scales them (see `body_scale`), so a bramblebun and a tuskroot each get a burst sized to their body rather than one fixed burst that swamps one and vanishes on the other. Colours are '#rrggbb'.
_comment_type_colours: The elemental hue a hit carries, keyed by the move's `type` in data/moves/moves.json. The move's own `vfx.colour` wins when it names one (every shipped move does); this map is the fallback for a strike that reaches the flash with only a type name, and the source of truth a designer edits to recolour an element everywhere at once. Values are the same swatches moves.json already uses.
_comment_tint_saturation: Multiplier on the saturation of whatever colour a hit arrives with (the move's own swatch or the type map) before it becomes a spark. moves.json's swatches were picked for a HUD hairline and are pale; 1.6 turns ground's tan into amber and water's sky blue into a real blue while air, which has almost no saturation to multiply, stays the pale it is meant to be.
_comment_damage_scale: How much bigger a heavy blow bursts than a light one. `fraction` is damage / the struck creature's max HP: at or below `light_fraction` the burst plays at `min`, at or above `heavy_fraction` at `max`, linear between. A charged move that takes a third of the bar should not look like a quick jab that took a twentieth.
_comment_burst_keys: `heat` is how white-hot a particle is born before cooling to its tint (0 none, 1 fully white at birth); `halo` the opacity of a darker, larger disc drawn behind each mote so it keeps an edge on bright ground (0 off). Shared by hit_spark, ko_puff and catch_burst (all scripts/vfx/vfx_burst.gd): `up_bias` tilts every particle's direction upward before normalising (0 isotropic, 1 mostly up); `grow` is how much a particle swells over its life (0 none, 1.2 more than doubles); `alpha` the peak opacity; `core_*` the bright flash at the origin that dies fast.
_comment_hit_spark: OFF by owner decision (2026-10-04): the shared spray read as a grey-brown haze burying every hit, and each move's own impact (move_library) now carries the contact. The block stays so the switch is data-only. The spark: a spray of bright motes and streaks thrown out from the point of contact, falling under gravity and fading. Lives longer than combat.json's 0.26s ring on purpose -- the ring says 'contact', the spray is what is still on screen a third of a second later. `count` is per burst; `speed` metres/second; `spread_degrees` the cone around the camera plane the sprays leave in; `size` the mote radius in metres; `streak_fraction` how many of them are drawn as elongated streaks along their own motion rather than round motes.
_comment_hit_flash: A RIM, not a flood. `flat_mix` was raised to 0.7 once and a blind round reported the body "flooded with a flat gold-amber tint" that "erases the separation between shell plate and fur" -- at a high flat mix the overlay stops being a light on the creature and becomes paint over it, and it made being hurt and being rewarded the same picture. Keep it low; the fresnel is what should carry it. The struck body lights up for a few frames: a material overlay drawn over every mesh of the creature, brightest at the silhouette (fresnel) so the flash reads as the body being lit rather than as a white blob painted over it. Per-instance (GeometryInstance3D.material_overlay), so two creatures of one species never flash together the way a shared-material edit would make them.
_comment_ko_puff: The creature that just fainted lets out a soft cloud: slow, pale, mostly upward, bigger and longer than a hit. Fired from the same damage hook as the spark, on the blow that emptied the bar, so a trainer's second creature falling mid-battle puffs the same as a wild one ending the fight.
_comment_catch_burst: The seal, on top of catching.json's own warm flash: gold sparkles thrown out from the sealed orb and drifting up, so a catch lands as a reward and not only as a verdict line.

catch_burst._why_n14:
N14-ROUTED-FOLLOWUPS, 2026-09-05, on N07-VFX-POLISH's routed finding: 'vfx.json catch_burst throws 26 dark-haloed motes from the orb; at three ticks they are still packed on it and the round-1 judge read them as dust or mud kicked up, burying the orb.'

The first attempt at this was WRONG and the arithmetic is why, so it is recorded: raising `speed` and WIDENING `speed_variance` moves the leading edge and leaves the slow tail exactly where it was, and the slow tail is what sits on the orb. `vfx_burst.gd` places a mote at `speed * (1 +- variance) * duration * (1 - (1 - u)^2.2)`, so at three ticks (u = 0.05, eased 0.107) the SHIPPED burst put its slowest motes 0.224 m from the orb centre -- deep inside a 0.60 m orb (`catching.json::throw.radius`), which is the pile-up the judge saw -- while its fastest were already 0.672 m out and clear. It was never a burst that failed to leave; it was a burst whose slowest third never left.

So `speed` 4.2 -> 8.1 and `speed_variance` 0.5 -> 0.30, which RAISES the floor rather than the ceiling: the slowest motes now stand 0.605 m out at three ticks, on the orb's rim rather than inside it, and the fastest at 1.124 m. `count` 26 -> 16 thins what is over the orb at any instant. `duration`, `size`, `halo`, `heat`, `streak_*`, `gravity` and both colours are untouched, so it is W09's own sparkle, thrown harder and thinner.

What this trades: at 8.1 the motes leave the resolve camera's frame sooner, so the sparkle is briefer. That is the priority N07's own round-2 judge already set on this composite when it ranked the orb's legibility above the ring's persistence -- 'every extra tenth of a second is a tenth of a second the orb is veiled'.

_comment_level_up: The reward picture. On the creature that levelled: a vertical column of light through the body, two rings that rise from the feet past the crown, gold motes climbing with them, and a rim glow on the body itself, all over `duration` seconds. Sized off the body's own height and radius so it fits whoever levelled. `bench_on_trainer` false means a party member that levelled in its orb (the bench share) gets no world flourish -- the HUD line still names it; there is no body to light. `min_gap` collapses a poll detection and a progression-feed event for the same creature into one flourish once Game.progression_feed exists.

move_library._comment: F25 draft remains flag-off until real player paths, visual judgment and Medium frame-time proof pass. Presentation never owns damage; host receipt travel_seconds wins. Guard flash is visual only.

ultimate_overrides._comment: Owner direction 2026-10-04: signature ultimates draw as big element-true effects (water: a crashing wave or a water ball like the fireball; the other uniques as the owner approved) depending on the move, drawn by this library through ultimate_library.launch. Breakthroughs select the growth tier.
